title: Behçet’s disease
diseaseDescription: Bounded human Behçet disease overview: HLA/ERAP1 and cytokine-locus susceptibility, T-cell and neutrophil activation, NET/coagulation and endothelial injury, plus mucocutaneous, ocular, vascular, neurologic, joint and intestinal branches. Primary-report associations, culture mechanisms and intervention populations remain distinct. Excludes monogenic mimics, diagnostic criteria and comprehensive treatment guidance.
releaseNote: Overall scientific summary of behcet-disease-appraised-candidate-83c3910e36e4; external current-literature review remains pending. Provisional automatic appraisal of behcet-disease-therapy-candidate-20261017-001. Automatic conservative metadata appraisal. Source entailment, study quality, broad disease coverage, circuit causation and independent replication require review. Confidence is capped at 1/4 until explicit editorial appraisal; therapeutic categories describe curated target coverage, not efficacy. No calibration or human approval is asserted. Independent review and calibration remain pending.

mapViews.label: Behçet disease: susceptibility, immune activation & organ injury

scientificSummary.scope: Bounded human Behçet disease overview: HLA/ERAP1 and cytokine-locus susceptibility, T-cell and neutrophil activation, NET/coagulation and endothelial injury, plus mucocutaneous, ocular, vascular, neurologic, joint and intestinal branches. Primary-report associations, culture mechanisms and intervention populations remain distinct. Excludes monogenic mimics, diagnostic criteria and comprehensive treatment guidance.

paragraphs.text: Circulating NET markers were higher in active than inactive disease and healthy donors. A selected vascular cohort included 23 Behçet patients with nonpulmonary aneurysms. Purified Behçet neutrophils exhibited spontaneous NET formation compared with healthy donors.

These selected findings describe a bounded candidate, whose overall explanation has not been independently checked against current literature. Abstract-level inspection; selected study population or assay, not proof of a universal disease mechanism. Selected clinical cohort; no population prevalence or molecular cause established. In the 207-person phase 3 trial, apremilast reduced oral-ulcer burden over 12 weeks versus placebo; major-organ involvement was excluded. Drug targeting and approval do not establish every proposed mechanism or benefit in every phenotype.
